# fleet-bench

> Benchmark harness for local LLM lanes and router fair-share validation.
> Parses lane profiles from TOML, runs CI-safe OpenAI-compatible chat
> completion probes, and aggregates latency, status, and token-throughput
> results.

## Overview

- Name: fleet-bench
- Purpose: Benchmark harness for validating local LLM inference lanes and router fair-share queuing; runs CI-safe completion probes and reports latency/throughput metrics.
- Language(s): Go
- License: MIT
- Authoritative README: <https://github.com/nfsarch33/fleet-bench#readme>
- Source of truth branch: `main`

## Quick Start

- Build and test:
  ```
  make test
  make vet
  make lint
  ```
- Minimum runtime prerequisites: Go 1.22+

## Key Concepts

- Lane profiles defined in TOML files
- CI-safe OpenAI-compatible chat completion probes
- Latency, status, and token-throughput aggregation
- Sentrux quality gate: `make sentrux`

## Runnable Examples

- Run tests: `make test`
- Run quality checks: `make vet && make lint && make sentrux`

## Related Repos

- [llm-cluster-router](https://github.com/nfsarch33/llm-cluster-router) — the router whose fair-share queuing this harness validates

## Operational Notes

- Issue tracker: <https://github.com/nfsarch33/fleet-bench/issues>
